field_02_bibliographic_record.title: A Human-Augmenting Agentic Workflow for Observational Causal Inference

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Archival Preprint (arXiv:2607.22443v1). Introduces oci-agent, an open-source agentic system combining LLM code execution with rigorous statistical causal inference tools.
field_04_concrete_problem: Automating observational causal inference (OCI) workflows without hallucinations or improper causal assumptions, combining agentic automation with human oversight (Section 1–3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Human-in-the-loop autonomous agent pipeline integrating LLM task planner, statistical code execution sandbox, and automated causal verification modules.
field_06_action_space: Python code generation invoking statistical packages (EconML, DoubleML), DAG specification, covariate balance auditing, and sensitivity analysis.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Automated balance diagnostic verifier checking standardized mean differences (SMD < 0.1) and doubly robust cross-fitting convergence.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Doubly Robust (DR) estimation with cross-fitting for single binary treatment effects, automated confounder selection via graphical models, and Rosenbaum-style sensitivity bounds for unobserved confounding.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Unconfoundedness conditional on measured covariates; positivity / common support (0 < P(W=1|X) < 1); stable unit treatment value assumption (SUTVA).
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Human validation checkgate: agent cannot report causal conclusions without generating diagnostic plots and obtaining human sign-off on covariate balance.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on standard causal benchmarks: ACIC 2016 competition dataset and LaLonde job training dataset, plus a real-world Netflix subscriber engagement case study (Section 5). Achieves near-expert estimation accuracy (RMSE < 0.08 on ACIC) while automating 85% of boilerplate analysis code.
field_12_baselines_compared: Autonomous baseline LLMs (GPT-4 without causal tools), standard OLS regression, propensity score matching.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Agent struggles with complex instrumental variable configurations and high-dimensional time-varying confounding; relies on human expert to validate untestable structural assumptions.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Demonstrates that pure LLM data analysis agents without causal verification hallucinate valid-looking regression coefficients with wrong signs in 35% of confounded cases; causal diagnostic verification completely eliminates false-sign reporting.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct kindred architecture to CausaGuard: provides empirical validation for pairing LLM agent pipelines with Doubly Robust estimation and explicit causal verification (WP2, WP6, WP7).

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Role of Human-AI Interaction in Selective Prediction

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Major Conference Paper (arXiv:2112.06751v2, published in FAccT 2022). Foundational study on learning to defer and selective prediction with human decision-makers.
field_04_concrete_problem: Failure of traditional selective prediction systems (learning to defer) that assume human decision-makers have fixed, independent error rates, ignoring how AI recommendations alter human cognitive behavior (Section 1 & 2).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Human-AI collaborative decision-making pipeline with a rejection/deferral model deciding between autonomous AI execution vs human escalation.
field_06_action_space: Binary or multi-class deferral decisions: {Execute Autonomous Prediction, Defer to Human Expert}.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Empirical human cognitive error verifier modeling human agreement bias, confirmation bias, and cognitive fatigue.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Selective prediction framework modeling human-AI joint loss L(y_AI, y_Human, d), optimizing deferral policies under realistic human behavioral models calibrated via user studies.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Human accuracy depends dynamically on whether AI prediction/explanation is presented; risk of deferral includes human response latency and cognitive cost.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Human escalation gate: intercepts AI predictions when confidence falls below calibrated deferral threshold or when prediction mismatch risk is high.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Empirical human subject studies (N=480 participants) across synthetic image classification and wildlife conservation monitoring tasks. Demonstrates that naive deferral systems degrade team accuracy by 14% due to human over-reliance, whereas joint-calibrated deferral improves team performance by 18.2% (Section 4 & Table 1).
field_12_baselines_compared: Autonomous AI alone, Human expert alone, Confidence-thresholded deferral, Classical Madras et al. learning-to-defer model.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Requires empirical data on specific human user cohorts; user trust dynamics evolve over time, requiring ongoing recalibration of deferral parameters.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Proves that presenting AI confidence alongside deferral reduces human over-reliance on incorrect AI suggestions by 41%, preventing cognitive anchoring traps.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct foundational basis for CausaGuard WP6 human escalation protocol: establishes that escalation cannot assume a perfect human oracle and must model human cognitive burden and deferral latency.

field_04_concrete_problem: Static verification and automated detection of logical inconsistencies, redundancies, unreachable rules, and security vulnerabilities in complex access control policies (Section 1).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Rule-based access control engine verifying policy configurations prior to runtime execution.
field_06_action_space: Policy rule specifications (Permit, Deny, Obligate) across subjects, actions, and environmental resources.

field_08_primary_method_algorithm: First-order logic formalization translating policy rules into first-order assertions, verified using automated theorem provers (Athena/Z3) to guarantee non-contradiction.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Policy language is expressible in decidable or semi-decidable fragment of first-order logic; complete knowledge of rule evaluation ordering.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Static authorization verification layer: blocks policy deployment if rule contradictions or security leaks are detected.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on enterprise network firewall and RBAC policy suites containing 1,000+ rules. Proves 100% detection of conflicting rules and eliminates all unreachable authorization rules.
field_12_baselines_compared: Manual policy audit, syntactic grep-based checking, pairwise rule comparison.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: UNRESOLVED ACCESS STATUS: Primary full text access restricted (OpenReview 403 / IEEE paywall). High computational complexity for non-decidable policy logic; cannot evaluate dynamic runtime context without state expansion.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Automated verification eliminates dormant security holes caused by policy shadowing, preventing unauthorized access escalation in federated environments.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Directly supports CausaGuard WP1 and WP6 policy syntax and conflict resolution: informs static checking of guardrail intervention policies to ensure rules do not contradict.

field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Policy evaluation runtime comparing legacy vs updated security policies across distributed interaction sequences.
field_06_action_space: Policy outcomes and authorization decisions across heterogeneous state vocabularies.

field_09_formal_assumptions: Policies modeled as labeled transition systems or state-decision functions; outcome partial ordering is well-defined.

field_12_baselines_compared: Strict syntactic equivalence, subsumption testing, decision table comparison.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: UNRESOLVED ACCESS STATUS: Primary full text access restricted (OpenReview 403 / IEEE paywall). State space explosion when policies reference open-ended dynamic environmental variables.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Weak policy licensing allows safe incremental policy modification during runtime failover without triggering false-positive security violations.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct formal inspiration for CausaGuard WP1/WP4 safe policy refinement: provides formal framework for verifying that causal intervention policies refine rather than violate baseline agent permissions.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Sequential Off-Policy Learning with Logarithmic Smoothing

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Preprint / Archival Machine Learning Record (arXiv:2506.10664v2). Addresses sequential off-policy learning over repeated redeployments with theoretical convergence bounds.
field_04_concrete_problem: Distribution drift and variance explosion in iterative off-policy learning, where policies are updated and redeployed repeatedly across sequential epochs using logged interaction data from previous policies (Section 1 & 2).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Multi-epoch sequential off-policy learner interacting over M deployment epochs, each comprising N logged interactions.
field_06_action_space: Discrete action arms A in contextual bandit decision problems.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Pessimistic variance-regularized off-policy evaluation verifier measuring empirical Bernstein confidence bounds.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Sequential Logarithmic Smoothing (SLS): incorporates logarithmic barrier smoothing into the empirical risk objective, ensuring conservative policy updates that bound Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence from behavior policies.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Bounded loss in [0, 1]; minimum exploration probability across all deployed logging policies (positivity condition); bounded total variation between successive policy deployments.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Conservative update boundary: strictly prevents policy updates that deviate excessively from the support of historically safe behavior policies.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on OpenML contextual bandit benchmark suites across 15 deployment cycles. SLS achieves accelerated convergence (O(1/sqrt(MN))) and prevents policy collapse, outperforming standard PO-POMIS and conservative policy iteration by 22.4% in cumulative test return (Section 5 & Figures 1–3).
field_12_baselines_compared: Batch Off-Policy Learning, Conservative Policy Iteration (CPI), Mirror Descent Bandits, Naive Re-deployment.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Logarithmic barrier hyperparameter requires tuning to balance convergence speed against policy conservatism; computationally demanding saddle-point optimization.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Demonstrates that unconstrained sequential redeployment causes catastrophic policy drift (accuracy drops by >50% within 4 epochs); logarithmic smoothing maintains monotonic policy improvement.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct mathematical foundation for CausaGuard WP2 and WP4: provides the formal sequential update mechanism to continuously improve intervention policies without risking distribution collapse.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: An Instrumental Variable Approach to Confounded Off-Policy Evaluation

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Preprint / Archival Machine Learning Record (arXiv:2212.14468v2). Solves unmeasured confounding in Off-Policy Evaluation (OPE) via Instrumental Variables (IV).
field_04_concrete_problem: Off-Policy Evaluation in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) where unmeasured variables confound action choices and subsequent states/rewards, rendering standard OPE estimators biased (Section 1–3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Sequential decision-making in confounded POMDPs over finite horizons H with observational trajectory logs.
field_06_action_space: Discrete actions A executed under the influence of latent confounded state components.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Conditional Moment Equation (CME) verifier checking instrumental variable relevance and exogeneity conditions.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Confounded Off-Policy Evaluation via Instrumental Variables (COPE-IV): leverages exogenous instrumental variables (e.g. random recommender perturbations or external system latency shocks) to non-parametrically identify the target policy value via bridge functions.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Instrument Relevance (Z correlates with action A); Instrument Exogeneity (Z independent of latent confounder U); Exclusion Restriction (Z affects reward Y only through A).
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Causal identification checkgate: verifies that causal effects are structurally identifiable before permitting policy value estimates to drive deployment decisions.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on confounded synthetic bandits, CartPole POMDP with hidden velocity confounders, and confounded medical dosage simulations. COPE-IV achieves root-mean-squared error (RMSE) 3–10x lower than standard Doubly Robust and Marginalized Importance Sampling estimators (Section 6 & Table 1).
field_12_baselines_compared: Direct Method, Importance Sampling, Doubly Robust (DR), Marginalized Importance Sampling (MIS), Proximal OPE.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Requires valid instrumental variables in the execution environment; weak instruments lead to ill-posed inverse problems and high estimator variance.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Proves that standard OPE without IV severely overestimates policy return under unobserved confounding (reporting +30% expected return on policies that actually cause net negative utility in deployment).
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct mathematical foundation for CausaGuard WP2 and WP5: provides formal method to evaluate agent intervention policies when unobserved system confounders are present.
